content.title: About
content.content: Crunch Cereal is a ready‑to‑eat breakfast made from whole grains that are toasted to a golden crisp. It has a light sweet flavor, a crunchy texture, and is suitable for both children and adults.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cereal is produced from a blend of wheat, oats and rice that undergo a double‑toast process.
It is often fortified with B‑vitamins and iron to boost nutritional value.
The first commercial crunchy cereal appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
There are more than 30 flavor variants, ranging from classic honey to chocolate.
Packaging is usually aluminum‑laminated to protect against moisture and preserve crunch.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: The cereal provides slowly digestible energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 aid nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Most varieties contain less than 2 g of fat per 100 g.

items.title: Fortified with minerals
items.content: Iron and zinc are commonly added to support immune health.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some flavored versions may contain up to 15 g of sugar per 100 g, which can be problematic for diabetics.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The product typically contains wheat, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Trace amounts of nuts, soy or dairy may be present due to shared manufacturing lines.

items.title: Loss of crunch
items.content: If left open, the cereal can become soft and lose its characteristic texture.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Crunch Cereal with milk, yogurt or a plant‑based beverage. It can be added to smoothies, used in baking, or topped with fruit and nuts for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cereal in its original sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer to an airtight container to maintain freshness.
